text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Pakistan and India have agreed to continue a dialogue on all outstanding issues including Kashmir and to prevent hostile propaganda and provocative actions against each other.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif described the Pakistan-India agreement on formation of working groups to solve key problems including Kashmir dispute as a major breakthrough.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto criticised what she called the government's "unfounded jubilation" over the outcome of the secretary level talks between India and Pakistan.
- Al Baraka group has acquired Muslim Commercial Banks's stake in Paramount Leasing Company.
- The Central Board of Revenue is facing a wave of hostility from industrial depositors over 1996/97 (July-June) tax deposits.
- The newly elected executive committee of Pakistan Banks Association has urged the State (central) Bank of Pakistan to set up a much-needed local clearing house for dollar accounts.
- The first open-end mutual fund in the private sector will be launched in three weeks with seed money of 325 million rupees.
- The National Bank of Pakistan and Dubai Islamic Bank have arranged $50 million for the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resoruces to finance oil imports.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- Prolonged power cuts in the sweltering heat crippled business activity in Karachi and the Karachi Stock Exchange suspended trading on Monday as members and agents walked out of the oven-like rings in protest.
- To protect local industry and stabilise sugar prices, the government has decided to stop sugar imports by the state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan.
FINANCIAL POST
- The Board of Investment is negotiating a $1.6 billion investment with Supavari Finance and Holding Company to set up an oil refinery in Pakistan.

- The government will spend 247.8 billion rupees on servicing of its domestic as well as foreign loans in the next financial year, showing an increase by 49.3 billion from the current year's revised expenditure of 198.5 billion.
THE NEWS
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif constituted a special committee headed by Interior Minister Shujaat Hussain to establish peace in Karachi.
- The chairman of the Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front, Amanullah Khan, called the agreement between India and Pakistan as the worst since the Shimla agreement signed in 1972.
THE MUSLIM
- Chief Minister Balochistan Sardar Akhter Mengal threatened to cut off gas supply to Punjab if wheat supply to his province was not restored.
THE NATION
- The Election Tribunal of Peshawar High Court headed by Mr. Justice Qazi Muhammad Farooq Pasha disqualified two ruling party senators and directed fresh elections on those seats.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
